title: Docs ↔ Code reconciliation
note: Every row compares what the NEW documentation asserts against the actual source in master-ronix/Dumby-Suite (apps/main at 9949df9cde8e7d858c65f4012fdea9124aad98ab, branch feature/dev). Standing rule: the specification is authority; where the code is narrower, the code is the gap to close. The anchor is the last commit to touch apps/main|packages, so no commit after it can move the code under a row without the freshness gate failing. Re-anchored 2026-10-27 to the module-boundary code change (UR-20261027-105): the loader, the module-system and the swastik surface moved, so every row was re-read against the new anchor; no existing row's subject changed, and REC-039 is added for the isolation claim.

facts.doc_claim: hash-bound provenance verification against the build record is the enforced floor, and the promoted artifact is verified before import (spec/governance/part-4-module-system-framework.md rule D-4.10; spec/modules/swastik-hot-reload-dynamic-module-management.md §15.8/§15.9)
facts.code_truth: the loader requires a build-provenance sidecar (no sidecar -> refuse), verifies the on-disk artifact hash against the builds row (L1, always), refuses a revoked build, and verifies the Ed25519 signature (L2, mandatory — no armed verifier -> refuse); bootstrap supplies the build store unconditionally and arms the verifier from BUILD_SIGNING_*
facts.resolution: Resolved by UR-20261019-101/103 (re-verified): the D-4.10 hash-bound floor always runs when a build store is supplied, and the signature layer is mandatory — the loader no longer imports an unverified module. Previously recorded as a code-gap (fail-open); the floor now holds.

facts.area: module ownership — one read for every surface
facts.doc_claim: every page and the install path read a module's holder from the ONE ownership resolver; no surface caches it or re-derives it (spec/modules/module-tiers-lifecycle.md)
facts.code_truth: page-data reads the holder fresh on every render — there is no process-lifetime memo; /browse marks a module occupied only when a DEFINED holder is not the acting profile; /health takes its held set from the ownership read for every profile, hosted or not; /modules and /dashboard use the same resolver
facts.resolution: Established by UR-20261026-097 (RT-1 … RT-3); the surfaces previously disagreed because four independent reads of one fact existed.

facts.area: module disable — command removal is queued, never immediate
facts.doc_claim: §17.7: a module disable's command removal never takes effect immediately at the registration layer; it is an entry in the shared guild command change queue
facts.code_truth: a disable writes the disabled state, writes the @everyone deny override that hides the commands instantly, and enqueues the removal; there is no per-command delete path (the applied===0 fallback was removed)
facts.resolution: Established by UR-20261026-097 (RT-4). The removed fallback had been de-registering commands instantly, which is neither of the disable's two halves.

facts.area: command dispatch — a module and its commands belong to one profile
facts.doc_claim: a guild-scoped module and its commands belong to one profile, and a profile that does not hold the module does not answer its commands
facts.code_truth: assertPersonaOwnsCommand refuses with CommandScopeDeniedError('owned-elsewhere') when the resolver names a different profile — a cause of its own, not the 'out-of-scope' catch-all that also serves a DM, the wrong guild for an admin command and an unresolved tier. core and admin short-circuit as 'shared'; the holder answers her own command. The renderer maps the cause to the OUT_OF_SCOPE notice reason code, which states that another profile holds the module.
facts.resolution: Established by UR-20261026-100 (RT-8) on the operator's ruling, and refined by UR-20261026-102, which split the cause out of 'out-of-scope' and added OUT_OF_SCOPE as the fifteenth reason code. It had logged and proceeded, which let a stale registration answer for the wrong profile.

facts.area: interaction — a refusal is answered privately
facts.doc_claim: a refusal is for the member who tried it, so it is delivered privately (spec/request-layer/division-2-interaction-lifecycle-buffer-notices-components.md)
facts.code_truth: the module-refusal notice is delivered with interaction.followUp — a new, private message — and declares ephemeral: true; the read-only guard permits followUp only for a handler that sets allowFollowUp, and keeps reply and showModal blocked
facts.resolution: Established by UR-20261026-098 (RT-6). Riding editReply on a publicly acknowledged interaction made the card private in grammar and public in fact.

facts.area: command dispatch — an absent command is explained, not called unknown
facts.doc_claim: a refusal tells the member the truth about WHY: a module another profile holds is reported as held elsewhere, a module switched off for the guild as switched off, and only a command the platform does not know as unknown (spec/request-layer/division-2-interaction-lifecycle-buffer-notices-components.md)
facts.code_truth: a profile's registry is filtered to the modules she holds, so dispatch misses another profile's command; on a miss the router consults the unfiltered globalRegistry and answers MODULE_DISABLED when the module is off for the guild, OUT_OF_SCOPE when another profile holds it, and UNKNOWN_COMMAND only when the command is genuinely unknown. Core and admin short-circuit, because 'another profile holds it' about a shared command would be a lie.
facts.resolution: Established by RT-15. Before it, a persona answered UNKNOWN_COMMAND for a module the main bot was answering OUT_OF_SCOPE.

facts.area: module re-enable — both halves of a disable revert
facts.doc_claim: a disable has two halves, an instant permission restrict and a queued removal, and a re-enable reverses BOTH: the command is restored to its default permission state and the queued removal is revoked before its push (spec/request-layer/command-framework-routing-engine.md §17.7)
facts.code_truth: an enable rewrites the @everyone command permission to allow — the command's default state, since Discord publishes no DELETE for command permissions — and enqueueModuleCommandChanges soft-deletes any pending row carrying the contradicting action for the same command keys, guild and application, before writing its own. pendingEntries returns rows in createdAt order so the replay is deterministic.
facts.resolution: Established by RT-17 and RT-18. Before it, a module toggled twice inside the batch window left a pending removal beside a pending re-registration and the replay decided the outcome by row order.

facts.area: Module isolation — the claimed ServiceLocator tier-based access control
facts.doc_claim: documentation/overview/trust-security-reliability.md and documentation/overview/engineering-philosophy.md state that the ServiceLocator's tier-based access control prevents Marketplace modules from accessing Admin-tier services, and that it prevents a module from accessing services it has not declared as dependencies
facts.code_truth: there is no ServiceLocator in the code. Until c6859e0 the loader handed every module the raw DI container with all 22 core tokens, so a marketplace module could resolve core.Db and core.CommandRegistry exactly as a core module could. Since c6859e0 the loader hands a guarded container that enforces a tier -> capability map (standard/marketplace hold the baseline eight and are refused the rest), so tier-based refusal now exists — but declared-dependency enforcement does not: the manifest's provides/services fields are declared and never wired
facts.resolution: Recorded 2026-10-27 by UR-20261027-105 / MB-1. The tier-based half is now real and enforced at load time (guarded container, ModuleCapabilityDeniedError); the declared-dependency half is not, and wiring provides/services would create the cross-module coupling the same directive forbids — so the prose should be narrowed to what exists rather than the code widened to match it.

facts.area: Module ownership of implementation — the core modules carry no code
facts.doc_claim: documentation/overview/the-philosophy.md states that the commands which let a guild owner enable or disable features are themselves shipped as a module, that the service which persists per-guild settings is a module, and that moderation, welcome messages and logging configuration are all modules 'loaded through the identical manifest contract, the identical DI container, the identical lifecycle hooks a third-party author would use'; spec/modules/module-anatomy-manifest.md defines the eleven-folder module layout those modules are supposed to fill
facts.code_truth: each of the eight packages under packages/modules/ holds two .ts files, 45-101 lines: an index that declares one command, and a command handler whose whole body returns { page, data } supplied by the host. services/, jobs/, events/, repositories/, migrations/, ui/, tests/ and config/ contain only .gitkeep, and assets/ holds one icon.png. Every page's data gathering, every button and dropdown handler, BCCM, RBAC and the module views are implemented in the core base: apps/main/src/rendering/page-data.ts (1170 lines) carries health, dashboard, browse, modules, queue, permit and persona pages; interactions/core-frame.handlers.ts carries the install/uninstall/disable controls; module-system/module-view.ts, queue/, permissions/ and personas/ carry the rest. No module package references a page implementation at all.
facts.resolution: Recorded 2026-10-27 by UR-20261027-105. The doctrine says a module owns its code and a core module is a module like any other; today 'core module' is a manifest label over host code, which is the inversion the operator flagged. Extracting each page's gathering and each interaction handler into its own module, behind the capability surface (MB-1), is the code-track item; /dashboard is the reference slice.

facts.area: Deployment startup — the port is opened only after the module seed
facts.doc_claim: spec/lifecycle/ci-cd-pipeline.md and the deploy pipeline describe a service that becomes reachable on its platform port and then seeds the tier volumes; start-production.mjs states its own contract as 'the bot starts UNCONDITIONALLY'
facts.code_truth: apps/main/Dockerfile:84 runs scripts/start-production.mjs, which ordered migrate (spawnSync timeout 120000) -> spawn Swastik -> waitForSwastik (up to 60 x 1s) -> seed deployer and push seven bundles (SEED_BUDGET_MS 180000) -> only then spawn the bot, which is the process that binds API_PORT. Worst case before any bind is 360 s. The operator's deploy log shows the platform giving up at 321 s: 'Port scan timeout reached, failed to detect open port 8080' at 09:29:20 after seeding began at 09:23:59, then a restart at 09:38:43 that seeded again from browse - because volumesPopulated() never short-circuited on an empty volume.
facts.resolution: Resolved and CONFIRMED ON THE LIVE INSTANCE 2026-10-28. The deploy log shows the sequence end to end: 'start-production: holding port 8080 while the seed runs' at 22:49:15, eight modules pushed with fresh build IDs at 22:49:23-26, 'released port 8080' at 22:49:26, 'liveness-holder: holding port 8080 while bootstrap runs' at 22:49:40, 'bootstrap-stage: MODULE_READY / STARTUP_COMPLETE' at 22:49:47, and '==> Detected service running on port 8080' at 22:54:50. The operator's screenshot then shows /dashboard rendering its seven commands.

facts.area: Module page surface dropped by the volume loader
facts.doc_claim: A module that declares a page owns that page: definePage in its package, exported as `pages`, registered by the loader, dispatched by the host (UR-20261027-106).
facts.code_truth: apps/main/src/module-system/swastik-loader.ts built the LoadedModule field by field - commands, jobs, events, tasks, onLoad, onReady, onUnload - and never copied `pages`. Seven modules exported a page, built it and shipped it in a correct bundle, and the loader discarded it: the PageRegistry stayed empty, the host (whose own dashboard() had been deleted) resolved the page to nothing, and /dashboard rendered as a bare module name. The deploy was healthy by every measure available - port bound, eight modules pushed, degradedModules=[] - because the fault was between the bundle and the registry, where no gate looked.
facts.resolution: Fixed 2026-10-28: the loader copies `pages`, and scripts/check-module-packages.mjs (Gate 3d) now requires that every surface any module exports - commands, jobs, events, tasks, pages - is copied by the volume loader. Confirmed on the live instance: /dashboard renders its seven commands.

facts.area: Module-specific renderer schema living in the framework
facts.doc_claim: A module owns its surface end to end: it declares the data it needs, composes its page, and carries its own renderer schema. The framework renders what the module hands it (UR-20261027-106, extended by the operator 2026-10-29: 'no renderer schema ... in modules' is the complaint).
facts.code_truth: Three module-specific block builders live in apps/main/src/rendering/ and are imported by the framework's command router, which picks between them with a hardcoded nested ternary on the page shape: rendering/persona-blocks.ts (269 lines), rendering/health-blocks.ts (182), rendering/modules-blocks.ts (68) - 519 lines. Each imports the framework's emoji constants and customEmojiRef directly, so the schema and the emoji resolution both sit in the host while the module supplies only data.
